previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her seventh cycle of high-dose methotrexate for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. Due to recent high ostomy output and hypomagnesemia, she was initially hydrated with IV fluids and given IV magnesium replacement. Chemotherapy was delayed by one day due to worsening neutropenia, but proceeded when counts stabilized. Methotrexate was administered at 3.5 g/m² and well tolerated. Leucovorin rescue was started 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling below 0.05 before discharge. Stool studies were negative for infection. Her diabetes was managed by holding metformin during admission, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments, including a revised metformin dose and new magnesium supplementation, along with three doses of oral leucovorin.

and CNS involvement with left occipital mass S/P 4 cycles of

___ cycle of high-dose methotrexate.  
.  
# DLBCL with CNS involvement: Received high-dose methotrexate 
(3500 mg/m2; her dose has been reduced ___ mucositis in the 
past), followed by leucovorin rescue. Per onc notes, she will 
likely have a repeat MRI brain after this cycle to help make a 
decision about whether the treatment following this will be with 
R-CHOP or with more high-dose methotrexate. Pt was neutropenic, 
ANC 420 on the day of discharge, but she was without fever or 
other signs of infection. Pt was d/c home when MTX level < 0.05 
___. She will continue leucovorin for 2 more days. 
She was given prophylactic ciprofloxacin for 7 days.
